text: Testing is a vital part of software development, and it comes in several forms. Unit tests check small pieces of code, like a single function, to make sure they work correctly in isolation. Integration tests, on the other hand, ensure that different parts of a program work well together. Many developers use test-driven development, where you write the test before the actual code. This approach forces you to think about what the code should do first. While testing takes extra time, it builds confidence. Knowing that your code passes tests means you can make changes more freely, fix bugs faster, and release updates with less fear of breaking things.
